title: Finite complex construction: two-sided Markowitz LPR cleanup refactorization on U8 (-2,580 macros, -37,320 real prims per orientation, seed 30, no new kappa)
head: bc0140e016bd865fffc7fdf64e12158183d52339
body:
## Summary

- **Status:** Construction (`no new kappa`) + scoped negative finding
- **Track & Seed:** `20–39: Complex supplier: improve one specific circuit, frame schedule, decoder, or paid recursive profile` (OS random seed: **`30`**)
- **Base Commit:** `abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf`
- **Selected Frontier Certificate:** `certificates/selected-result.json` ($\kappa = 1661960547713947 / 10^{18} = 0.001661960547713947$, PR #942 on PR #869/#870 and PR #890 / PR #858; **untouched**)
- **Package:** `research/u8-cleanup-markowitz-lpr-seed30/`

### What Changed and Was Learned

In the selected U8 complex supplier word (`native/barch/FULL-WORD.json.gz`, content SHA-256 `090fd574747fbf9628e70cb9beb792732914cfa52e1df147579fe4dbccc68c5a`; `native/local/CANONICAL-WORD.json.gz`, content SHA-256 `24db880b7dab31e6af4eec8a1aba1bbbae29cd50d9a7b77cf0e9b571b3e5ae7c`), the `full_frame_cleanup` section (`canonical['cleanup']`, running at frame `1` = `FULL` on the $490$ `FULL`-ended non-target registers) was synthesized by `cold44x.py` via one-sided (row-only) Gauss-Jordan elimination (`high_inverse = "dyadic_sparse_Gauss_Jordan"`) on $M_{\text{after}} = M_0^{-1}$ in fixed register index order $c = 0, 1, \dots, 727$.

While $M_{\text{after}}$ has $9,430$ off-diagonal nonzeros, the target cleanup operator $M_0 = M_{\text{after}}^{-1} \in GL_{728}(\mathbb{Z}[1/2])$ itself has **only $2,844$ off-diagonal nonzeros**, all with numerators in $\{\pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 3, \pm 4\}$ and denominators in $\{1, 2, 4\}$. One-sided elimination in fixed index order caused severe fill-in ($6,105$ scalar macros, $68,714$ real-component primitives per orientation), coefficient blowup up to $\max |\text{num}| = 131,646$, and a $72$-bit peak prefix $L_1$ coefficient norm (`48299247708521178587951/16`) in the backward orientation.

Replacing one-sided Gauss-Jordan elimination with a **two-sided Markowitz $R^{-1} P L^{-1}$ Schur-complement factorization and Weyl-group signed cycle realization** (`seed = 30`, `trial = 16`, `swap_pen = 6`, `scale_pen = 0`) achieves the following exact improvements across the U8 complex supplier word while preserving all $728$ columns, native frames, paid recursive profile, and residual adapter recipes:

| `full_frame_cleanup` real primitives (per orientation) | `68,714` | **`31,394`** | **`-37,320` (`-54.31%`)** |
| `full_frame_cleanup` max $\|\text{numerator}\|$ | `131,646` | **`8`** | **`16,455.75x` smaller** |
| `full_frame_cleanup` max denominator | `64` | **`8`** | **`8x` smaller** |

| Emitted events per orientation (`LOCAL-CHECKS`) | `24,415` | **`21,835`** | **`-2,580` (`-5,160` pair)** |
| Emitted scalar macros per orientation (`LOCAL-CHECKS`) | `19,213` | **`16,633`** | **`-2,580` (`-13.43%`)** |

| Paid recursive child profile (`local_rank_mass = 5634`) | `{1:2548, 2:338, 3:446, 4:162, 5:72, 8:8}` | **`{1:2548, 2:338, 3:446, 4:162, 5:72, 8:8}`** | **Identical (`0` delta)** |

### Scoped Negative Finding (Candidate 1)

We also prove and verify (in `PROOF.md` Section 5 and `verify.py`) why reverting $m \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ helpers of the 4-helper group $G = \{659, 661, 662, 663\}$ in U8 from entrance frame $E_5 = [298, 170, 102, 30, 1]$ (dim 5) back to $E_4 = [298, 170, 102, 30]$ (dim 4) to fill T37 rank-1 idle slots fails: the 12 bipartite delivery gates `B[420..431]` into $D_G = \{656, 657, 658, 660\}$ split between $E_4$ and $E_5$, splitting the single rank-4 climb $1 \to 5$ on $D_G$ into $1 \to 4 \to 5$ and producing local profile deltas $\Delta(m=1) = \{1:+2, 2:+1, 3:+3, 4:-3\}$, $\Delta(m=2) = \{1:+2, 2:+2, 3:+4, 4:-4\}$, and $\Delta(m=3) = \{1:-1, 2:+4, 3:+4, 4:-4\}$, strictly worsening the complex moment at $b_{\text{front}}$.
